scenes.headline: How one map compares layers across 38 models
scenes.sub: jspace-open: Jacobian-lens directions, linear CKA, and a shared three-block layout.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Eclair! Can you compare a layer of Llama with a layer of Qwen? This map does, across thirty-eight open models. Here's how.

scenes.text: Compare layers by how they arrange tokens' steering directions, not by coordinates, and any two layers of any two models become comparable.
scenes.say: Here's the trick: don't compare coordinates. Compare how each layer arranges the vocabulary's steering directions. Then any two layers, from any two models, share one scale.

scenes.title: Filling one cell of the map

items.say: At each layer, the Jacobian lens gives every token a direction: the push that most raises the model's urge to say it.
Probe four thousand and ninety-six token strings that every tokenizer shares, one row each.
Center them, and tabulate which tokens' directions align with which. That's a fingerprint with no basis in it.
The cell is the cosine between two fingerprints: linear CKA. It ignores rotation and scale, so a twelve-layer GPT-2 can face a sixty-four-layer Qwen.

steps.label: One model against itself: sensory, workspace, motor
steps.say: Compare every layer of one model with every other, and bright blocks appear: a sensory front, a workspace middle, a motor tail.

steps.label: Two families, rescaled to relative depth
steps.note: geometry only; the causal tests were run on Claude
steps.say: Rescale two unrelated models to the same zero-to-one-hundred-percent depth, and a bright diagonal band appears: matching layers at matching depth.

scenes.title: Cross-model CKA, mean of 703 pairs
scenes.note: only +0.040 is specifically about depth; depth order holds at 0.83
scenes.say: How strong is it? Across seven hundred and three pairs, most similarity is a shared lexical floor. Matched depth adds only point zero four. What's shared is the order.

scenes.text: Open models share an itinerary more than a computation: three blocks, in order, at the same relative depth.

recap: Each token gets a steering direction per layer
CKA compares geometry, ignoring rotation and scale
Three blocks, in order, at matched relative depth
scenes.say: To recap: steering directions per token, geometry compared with CKA, and the same three-block itinerary across families.
